title: To repeal certain provisions relating to notification to Senate offices regarding legal process on disclosure of Senate data, and for other purposes.
official_title: To repeal certain provisions relating to notification to Senate offices regarding legal process on disclosure of Senate data, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Austin Scott (R-GA) with 39 cosponsors; the House-passed measure has moved to the Senate per the latest recorded action.
summary: Repeals Section 213 of title II of division C of the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026 — the provision that established notification requirements for Senate offices regarding legal process on the disclosure of Senate data — and all amendments made by that section.
brief: Wipes out Section 213 of the FY2026 continuing appropriations extensions act and the amendments it made, ending the Senate-notification regime it created around legal process on Senate data.

top_lines.headline: Section 213 Repealed
subs: Repeals Section 213 of title II of division C of the FY2026 continuing appropriations extensions act
The amendments made by that section are also repealed
The section is declared to have no force or effect

sections.label: Section 1 — Repeal of Senate Notification Requirements Relating to Legal Process on Disclosures of Senate Data

items.main: Repeals Section 213 of title II of division C of the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026, together with the amendments made by that section.
items.detail: The bill states that the repealed section and its amendments "shall have no force or effect." The bill contains no other operative provisions.

gaps: The bill repeals the underlying section without stating an alternative notification standard for legal process on Senate data.
The bill does not describe transitional treatment for any notifications already issued under the repealed section.
The bill does not fetch or restate the language of the repealed section, so its full scope is not visible in this Act's own text.
The bill provides no effective date and no severability clause.

removed: Section 213 of title II of division C of the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026, and all amendments made by that section

title: Reimbursable Screening Services Program Extension Act of 2026
official_title: To authorize an extension and expansion of the reimbursable screening services program of the Transportation Security Administration, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Andrew Garbarino (R-NY) with 1 cosponsor. Cleared the House per the latest recorded action; no Senate action is recorded yet.
summary: Extends and expands the Transportation Security Administration's reimbursable screening services program by amending subsection (e) of section 225 of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019. The program's authorization runs "through fiscal year 2031" instead of "through fiscal year 2026," and the participation cap moves from "not more than eight" to "not more than 14."
brief: Extends TSA's reimbursable screening services program from fiscal year 2026 through fiscal year 2031 and raises the participation cap from eight to 14.

top_lines.headline: Program Extended Through FY2031
subs: Amends section 225(e) of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019 (49 U.S.C. 44901 note)
Authorization runs through fiscal year 2031 instead of fiscal year 2026

top_lines.headline: Participation Cap Raised to 14
subs: "not more than eight" becomes "not more than 14"
Same subsection (e) of section 225 of the 2019 appropriations act

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "Reimbursable Screening Services Program Extension Act of 2026".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Extension and Expansion of Reimbursable Screening Services Program

items.main: Extension: amends subsection (e) of section 225 of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019 (Public Law 116-6; 49 U.S.C. 44901 note) by striking "through fiscal year 2026" and inserting "through fiscal year 2031."
items.detail: The five-year extension is the only change to the program's time horizon in this Act.

items.main: Expansion: further amends the same subsection (e) by striking "not more than eight" and inserting "not more than 14."
items.detail: The bill changes only that numeric cap; it does not further amend eligibility criteria in subsection (e).

gaps: The bill does not restate what the reimbursable screening services program does; that program is defined in the underlying section 225 of the 2019 appropriations act, which is not reproduced here.
The bill does not describe how the raised participation cap will be allocated among applicants or which entities are eligible.
The bill does not include a funding authorization or appropriation of its own.
The bill does not require any reporting to Congress on program utilization during the extended period.

modified: Section 225(e) of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019: authorization changed from "through fiscal year 2026" to "through fiscal year 2031"
Section 225(e) of division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2019: participation cap changed from "not more than eight" to "not more than 14"

title: Homeland Security Capabilities Preservation Reporting Act of 2026
official_title: To amend the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 to require recurring reports on the transition of jurisdictions no longer eligible for Urban Area Security Initiative funding, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA) with 2 cosponsors. Cleared the House per the latest recorded action.
summary: Amends paragraph (1) of section 7102(b) of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117-263) so that the report on jurisdictions no longer eligible for Urban Area Security Initiative funding must be produced "every three years thereafter," not just once within 18 months of that Act's enactment.
brief: Turns a one-time report on jurisdictions losing Urban Area Security Initiative eligibility into a recurring one issued every three years.

top_lines.headline: Recurring UASI Transition Report
subs: Amends section 7102(b)(1) of the FY2023 NDAA (Public Law 117-263)
Adds "and every three years thereafter" after "Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act"
Change appears in the matter preceding subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1)

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "Homeland Security Capabilities Preservation Reporting Act of 2026".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Reports on Transition of Jurisdictions No Longer Eligible for Urban Area Security Initiative Funding

items.main: Amends paragraph (1) of section 7102(b) of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117-263) by inserting "and every three years thereafter" after "Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act" in the matter preceding subparagraph (A).
items.detail: The bill makes no other substantive amendment; it does not change the report's contents or recipients, which are set by the underlying section 7102(b) of the FY2023 NDAA.

gaps: The bill does not restate what section 7102(b) of the FY2023 NDAA requires the report to contain, so the subject matter of the recurring report is not visible in this Act's own text.
The bill does not identify the recipient committees or set a public-release requirement.
The bill does not authorize any funding to support the recurring reporting requirement.
The bill does not establish a sunset for the new triennial reporting cycle.

added: "and every three years thereafter" inserted into section 7102(b)(1) of the FY2023 NDAA, converting a one-time report into a triennial one

title: FEC Administrative Improvements Act
official_title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to require electronic report filing for persons making certain electioneering communications and to permit political committees to make disbursements other than by check.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Joseph Morelle (D-NY) with 3 cosponsors. Cleared the House per the latest recorded action; no Senate action is recorded.
summary: Makes two changes to the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971. Section 2 amends 52 U.S.C. 30104(a)(11)(A)(i) so that the electronic filing requirement covers persons who "make[] electioneering communications," not just those making expenditures. Section 3 rewrites 52 U.S.C. 30102(h)(1) to let political committees make disbursements by means other than a check drawn on the committee's account.
brief: Requires electronic FEC filing for persons making electioneering communications and lets political committees pay by methods other than check.

top_lines.headline: Electronic Filing for Electioneering Communications
subs: Inserts "or makes electioneering communications" after "expenditures"

top_lines.headline: Disbursements No Longer Check-Only
subs: Amends 52 U.S.C. 30102(h)(1)
Strikes "except by check drawn on such accounts in accordance with this section"
Inserts "except from such accounts" in its place

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "FEC Administrative Improvements Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Requiring Electronic Filing

items.main: Amends section 304(a)(11)(A)(i) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (52 U.S.C. 30104(a)(11)(A)(i)) by inserting "or makes electioneering communications" after "expenditures."
items.detail: The bill does not otherwise change the electronic-filing regime in section 304; it only expands the class of filers covered by that clause.

sections.label: Section 3 — Permitting Political Committees to Make Disbursements by Methods Other Than Check

items.main: Amends section 302(h)(1) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (52 U.S.C. 30102(h)(1)) by striking "except by check drawn on such accounts in accordance with this section" and inserting "except from such accounts."
items.detail: The bill's new language keeps the account-based limitation but removes the requirement that disbursements be made specifically by check.

gaps: The bill does not specify which non-check payment methods are permitted or set FEC rulemaking on the point.
The bill does not restate the definition of "electioneering communications," which is set in the underlying Federal Election Campaign Act and is not reproduced here.
The bill sets no effective date, so the timing of implementation depends on the general rule for enactment.
The bill does not describe how the FEC's existing electronic-filing infrastructure will be adapted to the newly covered filers.

added: "or makes electioneering communications" added to 52 U.S.C. 30104(a)(11)(A)(i)
modified: 52 U.S.C. 30102(h)(1) reworded from "except by check drawn on such accounts in accordance with this section" to "except from such accounts"

title: Protect America's Workforce Act
official_title: To nullify the Executive Order relating to Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Jared Golden (D-ME) with 226 cosponsors — one of the largest cosponsor blocs in the batch. The House-passed measure has moved to the Senate per the latest recorded action.
summary: Section 2 declares the March 27, 2025 Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" of no force or effect and bars any federal funds from being obligated or expended to carry it out. Section 3 preserves any collective bargaining agreement in effect as of March 26, 2025 between an executive branch federal agency and an exclusive representative of federal employees through the stated term of that agreement.
brief: Nullifies the March 27, 2025 executive order excluding federal agencies from federal labor-management relations programs and preserves collective bargaining agreements that were in effect the day before the order.

top_lines.headline: Executive Order Nullified
subs: Applies to the Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" issued March 27, 2025
The order "shall have no force or effect"
No federal funds may be obligated or expended to carry it out

top_lines.headline: Existing CBAs Preserved
subs: Covers collective bargaining agreements in effect as of March 26, 2025
Agreements between executive branch federal agencies and exclusive representatives of federal employees
They have full force and effect through the stated term of the applicable agreement

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "Protect America's Workforce Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Nullification of Executive Order Relating to Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs

items.main: The March 27, 2025 Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" is declared to have no force or effect, and no federal funds may be obligated or expended to carry it out.
items.detail: The section identifies the order by title and issuance date but does not list which specific agencies or bargaining units it addressed.

sections.label: Section 3 — Collective Bargaining Agreements

items.main: Any collective bargaining agreement in effect as of March 26, 2025 between any executive branch federal agency and any labor organization that is an exclusive representative of federal employees has full force and effect through the stated term of the applicable agreement.
items.detail: The section fixes eligibility to the day before the executive order but does not distinguish among agencies or bargaining units.

gaps: The bill does not restate which agencies or units the March 27, 2025 executive order covered; the scope of what is being nullified is not described in the Act itself.
The bill does not address collective bargaining agreements negotiated after March 26, 2025 or renewals during the covered agreements' stated terms.
The bill does not provide a remedy or enforcement mechanism for actions taken between March 27, 2025 and enactment.
The bill does not set an effective date beyond the general rule for enactment.

added: Preservation of collective bargaining agreements in effect between executive branch federal agencies and exclusive representatives as of March 26, 2025, through their stated terms
removed: Force and effect of the Executive Order titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs" issued March 27, 2025, together with any federal funding to carry it out

title: Stop Foreign Funds in Elections Act
official_title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to apply the prohibition against contributions and donations by foreign nationals in connection with elections to contributions or donations in connection with ballot initiatives and referenda.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) with 2 cosponsors. Cleared the House per the latest recorded action.
summary: Amends section 319(a)(1)(A) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (52 U.S.C. 30121(a)(1)(A)) by inserting ", including a State or local ballot initiative or referendum or recall election" after "State, or local election." The amendment applies to contributions and donations made on or after the date of enactment.
brief: Extends the Federal Election Campaign Act's ban on foreign national contributions and donations to state and local ballot initiatives, referenda, and recall elections, applying to contributions made on or after enactment.

top_lines.headline: Foreign National Ban Extended to Ballot Measures
subs: Adds ", including a State or local ballot initiative or referendum or recall election" after "State, or local election"

top_lines.headline: Forward-Looking Effective Date
subs: Applies to contributions and donations made on or after the date of enactment

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "Stop Foreign Funds in Elections Act".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Prohibition on Contributions and Donations by Foreign Nationals in Connection with Ballot Initiatives and Referenda and Recall Elections

items.main: Amends section 319(a)(1)(A) of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 (52 U.S.C. 30121(a)(1)(A)) by inserting ", including a State or local ballot initiative or referendum or recall election" after "State, or local election."
items.detail: The bill does not modify any of the other elements of section 319, including the definition of "foreign national" or the range of covered persons; it only widens the list of election-related activities that the prohibition reaches.

items.main: Sets an effective date under which the amendment applies with respect to contributions and donations made on or after the date of enactment.
items.detail: The Act does not create a retroactive remedy; contributions made before enactment are not covered by the amended clause.

gaps: The bill does not restate the definition of "foreign national" used in section 319; the term's scope is set by the underlying statute, which is not reproduced here.
The bill does not create a new enforcement mechanism or private right of action for the expanded prohibition.
The bill does not preempt or accommodate state-level laws that already restrict foreign contributions to ballot measures.
The bill does not authorize any funding for Federal Election Commission implementation.

added: ", including a State or local ballot initiative or referendum or recall election" added to 52 U.S.C. 30121(a)(1)(A) — expands the foreign-national contribution/donation ban to those categories

title: To lower the age at which a minor may be tried as an adult for certain criminal offenses in the District of Columbia to 14 years of age.
official_title: To lower the age at which a minor may be tried as an adult for certain criminal offenses in the District of Columbia to 14 years of age.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Brandon Gill (R-TX) with 6 cosponsors. The House-passed measure has moved to the Senate per the latest recorded action.
summary: Amends two sections of the District of Columbia Official Code to lower the age at which a minor may be treated as an adult in criminal proceedings for certain offenses. In section 16-2301(3) the exclusion threshold moves from "sixteen years of age" to "fourteen years of age." In section 16-2307(a) the ages at which a minor may be transferred to a criminal proceeding drop from "fifteen," "sixteen," and "eighteen" to "fourteen" in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) respectively. The changes apply to criminal offenses committed on and after the date of enactment.
brief: Amends the D.C. Official Code to lower the age at which a minor may be excluded from Family Court jurisdiction, or transferred to a criminal proceeding, from sixteen/fifteen/eighteen to fourteen — applying to offenses committed on or after enactment.

top_lines.headline: Family Court Exclusion Age Lowered to 14
subs: Section 16-2301(3), D.C. Official Code: "sixteen years of age" struck and "fourteen years of age" inserted
In the matter following subparagraph (C): "the age of sixteen" replaced with "the age of fourteen"

top_lines.headline: Criminal Transfer Ages All Reset to 14
subs: Section 16-2307(a)(1): "fifteen" → "fourteen"
Section 16-2307(a)(2): "sixteen" → "fourteen"
Section 16-2307(a)(3): "eighteen" → "fourteen"

top_lines.headline: Applies Prospectively
subs: Applies with respect to criminal offenses committed on and after the date of enactment

sections.label: Section 1 — Lowering Age at Which a Minor May Be Tried as Adult for Certain Criminal Offenses in District of Columbia

items.main: Subsection (a) amends section 16-2301, D.C. Official Code, paragraph (3), by striking "sixteen years of age" and inserting "fourteen years of age," and by striking "the age of sixteen" and inserting "the age of fourteen" in the matter following subparagraph (C).
items.detail: The bill leaves the surrounding structure of paragraph (3) intact; only the two age references are changed.

items.main: Subsection (b) amends section 16-2307(a), D.C. Official Code, striking "fifteen" in paragraph (1) and inserting "fourteen," striking "sixteen" in paragraph (2) and inserting "fourteen," and striking "eighteen" in paragraph (3) and inserting "fourteen."
items.detail: All three paragraph-level age thresholds for transfer to a criminal proceeding are moved to the same fourteen-year figure.

items.main: Subsection (c) applies the Act and its amendments only to criminal offenses committed on and after the date of enactment.
items.detail: Offenses committed before enactment remain governed by the pre-amendment ages.

gaps: The bill does not restate which categories of offenses trigger the exclusion or transfer, since those criteria are set in the surrounding text of sections 16-2301 and 16-2307 rather than in this Act.
The bill does not modify the procedural safeguards that accompany a transfer determination in section 16-2307.
The bill does not address parallel age references elsewhere in the D.C. Official Code that govern juvenile custody, records, or sentencing.
The bill does not include an appropriation or resource plan for the D.C. courts or corrections agencies that would handle the change.

modified: Section 16-2301(3), D.C. Official Code: exclusion age reduced from sixteen to fourteen years
Section 16-2307(a)(1), D.C. Official Code: transfer age reduced from fifteen to fourteen
Section 16-2307(a)(2), D.C. Official Code: transfer age reduced from sixteen to fourteen
Section 16-2307(a)(3), D.C. Official Code: transfer age reduced from eighteen to fourteen

title: FAST VETS Act
official_title: To amend title 38, United States Code, to modify the conditions under which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs is required to redevelop the individualized vocational rehabilitation plan for a veteran, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-72 on January 20, 2026. Per the printed legislative history for H.R. 4446, the House considered and passed the measure on September 15, 2025 and the Senate considered and passed it on December 18, 2025.
summary: Modifies the redevelopment step of the Department of Veterans Affairs' individualized vocational rehabilitation plan process. Section 3107(b) of title 38, United States Code, is restructured so that after the required review, the Secretary either (A) redevelops the plan when the veteran's long-range rehabilitation goals are no longer feasible due to changes in the veteran's employment handicap and are likelier under a different plan formulated under subsection (a), or (B) disapproves redevelopment when the Secretary determines it is not appropriate.
brief: Amends 38 U.S.C. 3107(b) so that, after reviewing a veteran's vocational rehabilitation plan, the VA Secretary either redevelops it under specified conditions or disapproves redevelopment when not appropriate.

top_lines.headline: Restructured Redevelopment Decision
subs: Amends 38 U.S.C. 3107(b) (Section 3107 of title 38)
Existing review sentence becomes paragraph (1)
The prior second sentence is struck

top_lines.headline: Two-Path Determination
subs: Redevelop when long-range rehabilitation goals are no longer feasible due to changes in the employment handicap AND likelier under a different plan under subsection (a)
Disapprove redevelopment when the Secretary determines redevelopment is not appropriate

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "Focused Assistance and Skills Training for Veterans' Employment and Transition Success Act" or the "FAST VETS Act."
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Conditions Under Which Secretary of Veterans Affairs Shall Redevelop Individualized Vocational Rehabilitation Plan

items.main: Amends subsection (b) of section 3107 of title 38, United States Code, by striking "The Secretary shall review" and inserting "(1) The Secretary shall review"; by striking the second sentence; and by adding a new paragraph (2).
items.detail: The rewrite converts the existing single-sentence review requirement into a numbered paragraph (1) and clears out the prior second sentence, making room for the new determination framework.

items.main: New paragraph (2) directs the Secretary, on the basis of the review, to (A) redevelop the plan when long-range rehabilitation goals are no longer feasible due to changes in the veteran's employment handicap and are likelier under a different plan formulated under subsection (a), or (B) disapprove redevelopment when it is determined not to be appropriate.
items.detail: Both criteria in prong (A) — infeasibility due to changes in the employment handicap and higher likelihood under a different plan — must be met before the Secretary redevelops the plan.

gaps: The bill does not describe how the Secretary must document a determination that redevelopment is not appropriate.
The bill does not set a deadline within which the Secretary must act on the review before the veteran's plan status is resolved.
The bill does not create appeal rights specific to the new redevelopment or disapproval determinations.
The bill does not authorize additional funding for the vocational rehabilitation program to support the restructured review.

added: New 38 U.S.C. 3107(b)(2): two-path Secretary determination — redevelop under specified conditions or disapprove redevelopment when not appropriate
modified: 38 U.S.C. 3107(b): existing review sentence renumbered as paragraph (1)
removed: The prior second sentence of 38 U.S.C. 3107(b)

title: Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserves Tuition Fairness Act of 2025
official_title: To Amend title 38, United States Code, to direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disapprove courses of education offered by a public institution of higher learning that does not charge the in-State tuition rate to a veteran using certain educational assistance under title 10 of such Code, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-55 on December 12, 2025. Per the printed legislative history for H.R. 983, the House considered and passed the measure on April 7, 2025 and the Senate considered and passed it on November 20, 2025.
summary: Extends the Department of Veterans Affairs' in-State tuition disapproval regime in section 3679(c) of title 38, United States Code, to cover educational assistance under chapter 1606 of title 10 (Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserves). It inserts ", or chapter 1606 of title 10," after existing chapter citations in paragraph (1) and paragraph (6), adds a new subparagraph (E) covering individuals entitled to assistance under section 16131 of title 10, and makes conforming changes to subsection (e). The amendments apply to an academic period that begins on or after August 1, 2026.
brief: Extends the VA in-State tuition disapproval rule in 38 U.S.C. 3679 to Selected Reserves educational assistance under chapter 1606 of title 10, effective for academic periods beginning on or after August 1, 2026.

top_lines.headline: Chapter 1606 Added to the Disapproval Rule
subs: 38 U.S.C. 3679(c)(1): inserts ", or chapter 1606 of title 10," after the existing chapter list
38 U.S.C. 3679(c)(6): inserts ", or chapter 1606 of title 10" before the period at the end

top_lines.headline: New Eligible Individual
subs: 38 U.S.C. 3679(c)(2)(E): individual entitled to assistance under section 16131 of title 10

top_lines.headline: Effective for Academic Periods Beginning On or After Aug. 1, 2026
subs: Amendments take effect on the date of enactment
But apply with respect to an academic period that begins on or after August 1, 2026

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "Montgomery GI Bill Selected Reserves Tuition Fairness Act of 2025."
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Department of Veterans Affairs Disapproval of Courses Offered by Public Institutions of Higher Learning That Do Not Charge Veterans In-State Tuition Rate for Purposes of Selected Reserve Educational Assistance Program

items.main: Subsection (a) amends 38 U.S.C. 3679(c) by (1) inserting ", or chapter 1606 of title 10," after "chapter 30, 31, 33, or 35 of this title" in paragraph (1); (2) adding new subparagraph (E) to paragraph (2), covering an individual entitled to assistance under section 16131 of title 10; and (3) inserting ", or chapter 1606 of title 10" before the period at the end of paragraph (6).
items.detail: The three changes extend the disapproval rule to the chapter 1606 (Selected Reserves) program in title 10, while leaving the paragraph (2)(A)-(D) categories in place.

items.main: Subsection (b) makes conforming amendments to 38 U.S.C. 3679(e): paragraph (1)(A) adds ", or chapter 1606 of title 10," after "chapter 31, 33, or 35 of this title"; paragraph (1)(B) replaces "chapter 31 33, or 35 of this title" with "chapter 31, 33, or 35 of this title, or chapter 1606 of title 10"; paragraph (2) makes the same replacement.
items.detail: Subsection (e) references are updated so the covered-chapter lists stay parallel to the amended subsection (c).

items.main: Subsection (c) sets the effective date: amendments take effect on the date of enactment and apply with respect to an academic period that begins on or after August 1, 2026.
items.detail: The two-tier effective date lets institutions and the VA adjust before the change binds any given academic period.

gaps: The bill does not restate the in-State tuition disapproval rule itself; that mechanism is set by the surrounding text of 38 U.S.C. 3679, which is not reproduced in this Act.
The bill does not create a private right of enforcement for a Selected Reserves student denied the in-State rate.
The bill does not authorize additional funding for the VA's disapproval or oversight activities.
The bill does not describe how existing state residency policies at public institutions must be modified to comply.

added: New 38 U.S.C. 3679(c)(2)(E) — individual entitled to assistance under section 16131 of title 10
modified: 38 U.S.C. 3679(c)(1): chapter 1606 of title 10 added to the covered-chapter list
38 U.S.C. 3679(c)(6): chapter 1606 of title 10 added before the closing period
38 U.S.C. 3679(e)(1)(A), (e)(1)(B), and (e)(2): parallel additions of chapter 1606 of title 10 in the conforming list

title: Improving Care in Rural America Reauthorization Act of 2025
official_title: To reauthorize certain programs regarding rural health care.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Buddy Carter (R-GA) with 5 cosponsors. The House-passed measure has moved to the Senate and been placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar (General Orders, Calendar No. 377).
summary: Reauthorizes and adjusts three rural health grant programs administered under section 330A of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254c). Subsections (a) and (b) add a new paragraph (4) to sections 330A(e) and 330A(f), directing the Director, when awarding Rural Health Care Services Outreach Grants and Rural Health Network Development Grants, to ensure that funds are used to meet the health care needs of, and involve, rural underserved populations in the local community or region to be served. Subsection (c) amends section 330A(j) by striking "2021 through 2025" and inserting "2026 through 2030," reauthorizing the programs for the next five-year window.
brief: Adds a rural-underserved-population use-of-funds paragraph to two rural health grant programs in 42 U.S.C. 254c and reauthorizes the programs from fiscal years 2021 through 2025 to fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

top_lines.headline: Outreach Grants: Rural Underserved Populations Focus
subs: Amends section 330A(e) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254c(e))
New paragraph (4): funds used to meet the health care needs of rural underserved populations and to ensure their involvement in the project

top_lines.headline: Network Development Grants: Same Focus
subs: Amends section 330A(f) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254c(f))
New paragraph (4): funds used to increase access via integrated health care networks and involve rural underserved populations in planning, development, and ongoing implementation

top_lines.headline: Reauthorization Window Extended
subs: Amends section 330A(j)
Strikes "2021 through 2025"
Inserts "2026 through 2030"

sections.label: Section 1 — Short Title

items.main: Names the Act the "Improving Care in Rural America Reauthorization Act of 2025."
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Rural Health Care Services Outreach, Rural Health Network Development, and Small Health Care Provider Quality Improvement Grant Programs

items.main: Subsection (a) amends section 330A(e) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254c(e)) by adding a new paragraph (4) directing the Director, in awarding a grant under that subsection, to ensure the funds are used to (A) meet the health care needs of rural underserved populations in the local community or region to be served, and (B) support other activities that ensure the involvement of those populations in the development and ongoing operations of the project.
items.detail: The paragraph is a use-of-funds directive; it does not change the eligibility criteria or matching requirements that govern the grants elsewhere in section 330A.

items.main: Subsection (b) amends section 330A(f) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254c(f)) by adding a new paragraph (4) with the same structure — funds used to (A) increase access to quality health care services through integrated health care networks for rural underserved populations, and (B) support other activities to involve those populations in the planning, development, and ongoing implementation of the network.
items.detail: The Network Development Grants program picks up the same rural-underserved-populations focus, expressed in network terms.

items.main: Subsection (c) amends section 330A(j) of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 254c(j)) by striking "2021 through 2025" and inserting "2026 through 2030."
items.detail: The single-line reauthorization moves the covered fiscal years without changing the dollar authorization language in subsection (j).

underreported.section: Section 2 heading — Small Health Care Provider Quality Improvement
underreported.summary: The section heading names the "Small Health Care Provider Quality Improvement Grant Programs" alongside the Outreach and Network Development programs, but the operative text of subsections (a), (b), and (c) only amends section 330A subsections (e), (f), and (j) — no discrete change is directed at a Quality Improvement grant subsection.
underreported.why_unreported: The heading is broader than the operative changes; readers scanning the section title may expect provider-quality-specific edits that this Act does not include.

gaps: The bill does not restate the dollar authorization figures in section 330A(j); the reauthorization changes only the fiscal-year window.
The bill does not define "rural underserved populations" for purposes of the new paragraph (4) directives.
The bill does not require the Director to report to Congress on how funds are being used to reach the newly emphasized populations.
The bill does not modify the underlying eligibility criteria for either grant program in sections 330A(e) or 330A(f).

added: New paragraph (4) at 42 U.S.C. 254c(e) — Rural Health Care Services Outreach Grants use-of-funds directive for rural underserved populations
New paragraph (4) at 42 U.S.C. 254c(f) — Rural Health Network Development Grants use-of-funds directive for rural underserved populations
modified: 42 U.S.C. 254c(j): reauthorization window changed from fiscal years 2021 through 2025 to fiscal years 2026 through 2030
